actionResultText:
Here's your **Derivative Intuition Explorer**! 🎉

---

### How to use it

| Element | What it shows |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **Red point P** | Drag it left/right along $f(x) = x^3 - 3x + 1$ |
| 🔵 **Blue tangent line** | The **instantaneous slope** $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 3$ at P |
| 🟢 **Green secant line** | The **average rate of change** $\dfrac{f(x+\Delta x) - f(x)}{\Delta x}$ from P to Q |
| 🎚️ **Δx slider** | Shrinks the gap between P and Q |

---

### The Core Idea

As you **drag Δx → 0**, watch what happens:

$$\text{Secant slope} = \frac{f(x+\Delta x) - f(x)}{\Delta x} \;\xrightarrow{\Delta x \to 0}\; f'(x)$$

The green line **rotates into** the blue line — that limiting process *is* the derivative. The tangent line isn't drawn from the function itself — it emerges from shrinking the secant down to a single point. That's the whole insight!
